label: All projects
guide: Browse and select existing projects, including archived ones. Butler can create a new project with a managed workspace or ask the paired browser to choose a Nebula-host folder for a linked project. For an existing project, interactive Butler can prepare nebula.projects.relink after reading its current revision; the requesting browser chooses and confirms the new host folder. Core refuses relinking while old-workspace sessions or work can resume and reads back the saved path. Existing files remain in the old folder. Host access follows the project's existing one-time policy.

label: Evidence
guide: Butler can page selected-project Evidence metadata and read an exact record. For upload, the requesting browser chooses a local file up to 25 MB, reviews its title, type and project links, then verifies the saved hash and Core record. For original-file download, the browser confirms sensitive content and checks the Core revision and SHA-256 before starting a device download. Butler receives no file bytes; an uncertain upload requires inspection before retrying.

label: Results
guide: Butler discovers saved Results with nebula.data.results, reads metadata with nebula.data.result, and reads exact result or separate hints as bounded JSON chunks with nebula.data.read_result. It never executes the payload. nebula.data.delete_result asks this browser to confirm the exact title and revision, then reads Core absence and refreshes Results. A failed or uncertain readback requires inspection before retry.

label: Reports
guide: Butler can page the selected project's reports, inspect a saved revision and its source findings or notes, and ask this browser to create, edit, or confirm deletion of a draft or review report. Core checks the current revision and may retain a report referenced by a PDF render. For a linked note, Butler can prepare an exact-revision AI section transform; this browser selects a permitted runtime, asks before sending source content to a cloud runtime, and saves only the operator-reviewed draft after Core read-back. The source note remains unchanged. The Reports screen keeps final sign-off with the operator's own identity and attestation; signed final reports cannot be deleted. PDF and sensitive engagement bundle exports download only to the requesting device after browser confirmation; Butler receives no file bytes.

label: Chat
guide: Open Conversations, choose Select conversations, select individual chats or all matches, choose Archive, Restore, Pin, Unpin, Flag, Clear flag, or Delete permanently, then Apply. Core readback confirms each result; deletion requires operator confirmation. Butler can search visible saved project messages with nebula.data.search_chats, page current bookmark states with nebula.data.bookmarks, and set or clear a bookmark with nebula.data.set_bookmark using its current revision (zero for an absent record). Core verifies the saved state; the requesting chat refreshes its bookmark controls. Private Butler, side and temporary conversations are excluded. Use nebula.inspect.turns and nebula.inspect.chat for bounded Core context, reasoning, evidence, hooks and saved result projections. Tool output and search use Core redaction; original artifact bytes require a confirmed requesting-browser download. A saved source preview is explicit browser input and closing it attaches no excerpt.

label: Terminal
guide: Opening Terminal on this browser starts or reconnects the selected project's live shell. Interactive Butler can list ticket-free live session identities with nebula.terminal.list and request a stop for one exact session with nebula.terminal.stop. The requesting browser confirms the destructive stop, checks Core again, then reads back absence. Butler never receives WebSocket tickets or shell output. An uncertain stop requires fresh inspection before retry.

label: Browser
guide: Interactive Butler can page active sessions with nebula.work.browser_sessions and start a scoped passive-inspection mission through nebula.work.start_mission with exact targets and lease limits. Delegated browser work allows only the passive risk class and no new credential grants. Active testing and credential grants remain in the operator-controlled Browser. Core enforces project scope and creates the bounded lease. A saved mission ID is a start receipt; inspect mission status for completion.

label: Activity
guide: Butler can page execution history and current status with nebula.inspect.executions and nebula.inspect.execution, read verified redacted output with nebula.inspect.execution_output, and cancel one exact execution at its current revision with nebula.inspect.cancel_execution. Core confirms the actual status and refreshes Activity. Cancelling requires later terminal readback. Original artifact downloads require browser confirmation and integrity checks. Starting or rerunning code retains the operator review control.

label: Files
guide: Open the selected project's Files view to browse folders and verify saved entries. Butler can list exact directories, create or rename folders with current directory identities, request empty-folder deletion with confirmation, and ask this browser to choose a file for an authenticated upload. Device file bytes are never sent through Butler's tool result.

label: Settings
guide: For the paired terminal Assistant, nebula-core headless starts Core without a GUI or frontend build. Install the lightweight nebula-client Python package on Linux or macOS. On the Core host use nebula-core chat invite; the client runs nebula-chat pair, then nebula-chat or nebula-chat shell for a full-screen terminal Assistant with live progress, local LOADING feedback while opening a menu or selection, Core-backed RUN/WAIT/IDLE conversation status in the rail and F3 picker, searchable project/chat menus, direct main-agent conversations, one-turn skills, Core goals and immutable goal skills, next-turn model/tool settings, attachments, approvals, input, queues and schedules. Switching chats detaches output without cancelling Core work. The new shell needs Core terminal protocol 1; legacy chat resumes the project Butler conversation on older Cores. nebula-chat unpair revokes that terminal. See docs/CLI.md for HTTPS, private CA certificates and host-only invitation steps. Open Settings. For current Core CPU and available-memory pressure or queued-work reasons, interactive Butler discovers nebula.work.host_load; scheduled Nebula-wide Butler uses nebula.global.host_load. Each read calls authenticated /api/v1/host-load and reports sample_age_seconds from Core’s one-second shared sampler. Re-read after load changes; unavailable measurements remain unknown. Settings → Setup → CPU budget configures this Core host independently of other hosts. Read nebula.work.host_cpu_budget or scheduled nebula.global.host_cpu_budget, then Settings GET/PUT /api/v1/host-cpu-budget using host_id and expected_revision. Automatic uses half capacity; cpu_limit=null selects Automatic. Read back the saved policy and actual apply_state/applied_cpu_limit; saving an inactive policy does not enable the experimental shared executor. Settings → Setup → CPU budget also enables or disables one host-wide PDF worker pool on Linux. Use GET/PUT /api/v1/host-cpu-budget with fresh host_id/expected_revision and enabled only for an explicit activation request; omitting enabled preserves it. Read executor_state, apply_state and worker_count: saved/pending is not running, and disabled requires zero workers. Whole CPU workers use observed Linux affinity, Automatic roughly half with minimum one and maximum four. Resize/disable drains accepted work. This pool excludes external chat/tool/LLM/GPU processes; external quota backends cannot be activated here.
